I got into handloading the hard way. I mail ordered a kit and played with it.

Find someone locally who will teach you on their equipment first.

Then, order a kit with JUST WHAT YOU NEED, nothing fancy from MidwayUsa.com. I suggest Lee brand equipment. Maybe get 2 cheap "C" presses so you do not have to adjust your dies so often. Start with a pistol caliber because straight wall brass is easy to resize with carbide dies. Bottle neck rounds are harder. Start with FMJ projectiles that are the most common weight for that caliber. Buy enough components to make up 500-1,000 identical rounds. It is frustrating to mess up 10 rounds and then only make 10 good rounds. Pick you load data before buying any projectiles or powder.

Have your friend show you on your equipment. Have your friend help you test your first rounds. He will know what pressure signs to look for.
